test_constructorArgumentsChangeTheAddres.notice: Same salt, different constructor argument. The addresses must differ, because the constructor arguments are part of the init code, not the salt.

test_predictIsUsableBeforeDeployment().notice: The prediction must be callable before anything exists. If it were not, an address could not be known in advance and the whole point of CREATE2 would be lost.

test_rejectsRevertingConstructorCode().notice: Init code that reverts in its constructor (`fd` with no data). CREATE2 returns address(0), which must become a revert — returning 0 would hand the caller an address that was never deployed.

test_saltForCommitsToBothAssetAndInitCod.notice: The salt commits to the init code. Two assets with the same init code must still get different addresses, and the same asset must always get the same one.

test_secondDeploymentWithTheSameSaltReve.notice: Without this guard CREATE2 is not idempotent, it is deceptive: a second deployment with the same salt returns the address of the first contract and deploys nothing.

test_theDeployerIsPartOfTheAddress().notice: The deployer is part of the address, so the same salt from another factory lands elsewhere. A vanity address found for one deployment path is not valid for another.
